required_stages.description: Every call, inside run(), zero-fill the fp32 (M, N) accumulation target before the Stream-K wave (the output itself for fp32 inputs, a separate fp32 buffer for fp16/bf16).

A persistent launch of one program per SM covering the Stream-K region (remainder tiles plus one extra full wave when at least two full waves remain): the region's K-iterations are split into equal contiguous ranges, each segment is reduced in a local fp32 accumulator and added into the zeroed accumulator with fp32 atomic adds; no fixup kernel, semaphores or partials workspace.

The remaining full tiles, each reduced over the full K range by a single program (one or several tiles per program), fp32 accumulation and ordinary (non-atomic) stores into the accumulation target; launched only when such tiles exist. May be merged with the wave into one persistent launch.
For fp16/bf16 inputs only, one rounding of the fp32 accumulation target into the output tensor after both regions have completed.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The whole GEMM is performed by a PyTorch / library matmul.
The @ operator on tensors performs the GEMM in PyTorch.
A BLAS library or a global matmul-mode switch replaces or alters the kernel.
Possible cross-call cache keyed by input identity/data pointer; transformed operands must be rebuilt inside every run().
Transposing B: permitted only if performed inside run() on every call and never cached.
Semaphores, flags or a partials workspace indicate a non-canonical Stream-K fixup or a split-K scheme.
Half-precision atomic combination: partials must be combined in fp32 and rounded once at the end.
Disabling TF32 for fp32 operands is a different numeric mode from the canonical behaviour.
Mutating or returning an input violates the no-mutation / fresh-output rules.

required_evidence.message: No atomic-add fixup found; the Stream-K region must combine segments with fp32 atomic adds into the zeroed accumulator.
No per-call zero-fill of the fp32 accumulation target found.
No SM-count query found; the Stream-K partition must derive from the device's SM count.
No evidence of the Stream-K partition (remainder tiles, per-program iteration ranges).
No TF32 evidence for fp32 operands.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (M, N) tensor of the input dtype must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with a or b (for fp32 it may be the fp32 accumulation target itself)

timing_boundary.notes: The GPU time of all device work launched by run() on every call is counted: the zero-fill of the fp32 accumulation target, any operand re-layout copy, the Stream-K and data-parallel launch(es) and the final half-dtype cast. The SM-count query, the output allocation call and descriptor/metadata construction are host-side work and not GPU time. Decided rule: A and B are delivered row-major and may be consumed as delivered or through a transposed/repacked copy rebuilt by device work inside every run() (its time counted); cross-call caches of a transformed operand, descriptor or output keyed on input identity, data pointer, shape or contents are forbidden; no prepacked operand may be assumed. The Stream-K decomposition and the atomic-add global accumulation into the zero-filled fp32 target are the fixed structure. bytes_expr counts A, B and C once (lower-bound model); zero-fill, atomic read-modify-write, the half-dtype fp32 round trip and repack traffic are diagnostic. The manual Triton reference caches B^T untimed and is not comparable; the cuTile reference does not repack.
